content: Buflomedil is a vasoactive drug that has been utilized in the treatment of peripheral arterial diseases. Research has suggested that it may have potential benefits for individuals with cerebrovascular conditions, including acute ischaemic stroke. However, it has not been approved for clinical use in stroke treatment. The objective of this review was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of buflomedil in the management of acute ischaemic stroke. The review included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared buflomedil to placebo, buflomedil combined with standard medical care versus standard care alone, or buflomedil combined with another intervention versus that intervention alone. Trials comparing buflomedil alone to other active treatments were excluded. The primary outcome assessed was long-term death or disability/dependence. Secondary outcomes included short-term death, short-term disability, neurological deficits, and adverse events. Data were collected and analyzed by two independent reviewers, and meta-analyses were performed for death and neurological improvement using a random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on time since stroke onset, delivery method, daily dose, and treatment duration. A total of 26 trials involving 2756 participants were included, all conducted in China. Participants were hospitalized within the first few days after stroke onset, with a mean age ranging from 58 to 75 years and a male proportion of 45% to 80%. Most studies administered buflomedil intravenously at a daily dose of 200 mg for 14 days. The overall quality of the studies was poor, with many trials lacking adequate reporting. Only one trial reported long-term outcomes, showing that stroke survivors treated with buflomedil had a lower risk of death or disability compared to the control group (200 participants; risk ratio [RR] 0.71; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.53 to 0.94). However, there was no strong evidence for short-term outcomes, including death, disability, or neurological deficits, based on the available data. Adverse events were assessed in 17 trials involving 1899 participants. Six trials (853 participants) reported no significant adverse events, while 11 trials (1046 participants) documented 38 adverse events in the buflomedil group and two events in the control group. The quality of evidence for all outcomes was rated as low according to GRADE criteria. In conclusion, there is insufficient evidence to support the efficacy or safety of buflomedil for the treatment of acute ischaemic stroke. The findings highlight the need for a well-designed, adequately powered randomized controlled trial to further investigate the potential role of buflomedil in this context.
